video.title: Chicago Bulls 2026/27 NBA Season Preview: Matas Buzelis Breakout Incoming?

summary: Josh Lloyd and Hayes from Locked On Bulls preview the 2026/27 Chicago Bulls. The team has a new front office and new head coach Thiago Splitter, and it added Norman Powell, Nic Claxton and rookie Caleb Wilson (No. 4 pick), mostly on short, flexible deals. Matas Buzelis is expected to get more usage, shot volume and ball handling in year three after Billy Donovan kept him on a short leash. Josh Giddey is expected to be the main playmaker, with a target of top three in assists, though he needs to cut turnovers and stay healthy. Both are doubtful that Claxton can rebound from his decline. Leonard Miller is seen as ahead of Patrick Williams in the rotation. Hayes predicts 32 wins, and Josh says he wants to draft Buzelis and sees Wilson as maybe the No. 2 rookie.

rules.text: On thin non-playoff teams, an injury to a main player makes the depth a problem, and that affects the value of the players left.
rules.quote: it's going to come down to if you cop a serious injury to a main player because the Bulls I think are pretty thin

rules.text: Be careful with late-season usage spikes. They often come in meaningless games.
rules.quote: His usage went over 25% in a lot of those games that were meaningless

rules.text: Rebuilding teams that are not playoff threats give young players more opportunity because they want to find out what they have.
rules.quote: it's not going to be a playoff threat you you want to see what you got like

rules.text: Young players usually get more usage and minutes each year, from a small rookie role to a bigger role by year three.
rules.quote: that's just generally the progression for these sort of players and just get comfortable get comfortable with the line

rules.text: Hot summer league shooting percentages are not sustainable. The willingness to shoot is the more useful signal.
rules.quote: the percentage isn't 41% isn't going to be maintainable

player_notes.text: Last season under Billy Donovan he was on a short leash. He was benched after mistakes and played only about 26 minutes early in the season.
player_notes.quote: Bzelis does one thing and then he sits and he plays 26 minutes only

player_notes.text: Over the final 20 games he played 33 to 34 minutes and produced lots of blocks and threes.
player_notes.quote: the final 20 games or so we started playing 33 34 minutes. He blocked a ton of shots.

player_notes.text: New coach Thiago Splitter is expected to give him more ball handling and point forward duties.
player_notes.quote: I think we're going to see more more ball handling.

player_notes.text: His shot volume is expected to go up despite the Powell and Wilson additions.
player_notes.quote: No, I think the shot volume is probably going to go up.

player_notes.text: His usage should be lower than his late-season peak but higher than at the start of last season.
player_notes.quote: I don't think that use is going to be quite as high as the end of the season

player_notes.text: Josh wants to draft him, took him in a recent mock draft and expects a big season.
player_notes.quote: I hope I'm going to draft Matsilus. I drafted him in the mockdraft the other day.

player_notes.text: He will be the offensive hub but still needs to score around 15 to 16 points per game because the team lacks shooting.
player_notes.quote: he's probably still going to have to be around 15 16 points per game

player_notes.text: His three-point shooting has improved to about 37% and 36.5% over the last two seasons on low volume.
player_notes.quote: him shooting 37 and then 36 and a half% last season

player_notes.text: He is a high-usage passer with high turnovers, which he needs to lower.
player_notes.quote: I think he's going to have to also lower the turnovers.

player_notes.text: Availability is a concern. Hayes says he needs to play over 60 to 65 games.
player_notes.quote: Giddy has to stay on the court like he has to play over 60 65 games

player_notes.text: His rebounding and transition play remain strengths.
player_notes.quote: The rebounding is still going to be there. The transition play is still going to be there

player_notes.text: Hayes wants him top three in assists per game. Josh thinks he should be around 10 assists per game.
player_notes.quote: but he should be around that double digit mark for assists

player_notes.text: He is the only Bulls player paid over $20 million per year and faces the most pressure if the season goes badly.
player_notes.quote: he's the only player on the team over $20 million per year

player_notes.text: He signed a two-year deal with a team option in the second year, which makes him easy to trade.
player_notes.quote: Now, Norman Pal comes in two-year deal, team option, second year.

player_notes.text: He is the Bulls' main off-ball shooter. Without him they have almost no shooting.
player_notes.quote: if they don't have Norman Pal, they have almost no shooting

player_notes.text: Over the last two seasons he scored over 20 points on about 15 shots per game, but Hayes calls that not tremendous value.
player_notes.quote: last two seasons, he's averaged 15 and gotten over 20 points. But I that's not like tremendous value.

player_notes.text: He has declined over the last three years. Back problems and falling block and rim protection numbers raise doubts.
player_notes.quote: some of the back problems he had and the lack of um block numbers and even rim protection

player_notes.text: He fits a switching, blitzing defensive scheme. Brooklyn had pushed him out to the perimeter.
player_notes.quote: He can he can he can guard multiple positions. He can blitz. He can switch.

player_notes.text: He is on a two-year deal and will start at center in Chicago.
player_notes.quote: So, he's going to still come in here and start.

player_notes.text: Josh has low hopes because Claxton has looked disinterested and has struggled.
player_notes.quote: My hopes just aren't particularly high cuz I just seen him sort of be very very disinterested

player_notes.text: He entered the league seen as a lower-usage defensive prospect but showed offense and three-point shooting in summer league.
player_notes.quote: he came in with a reputation as a lower usage defensive prospect

player_notes.text: The Bulls are not expected to push his offensive role much as a rookie.
player_notes.quote: They're not going to try to push him to do too much offensively right away.

player_notes.text: Long term he probably leans more defensive than offensive, though the gap should narrow.
player_notes.quote: if you had to look at it in 5 years time and go what is Caleb Wilson I still say he probably leans better

player_notes.text: Josh currently projects him as maybe the number two rookie.
player_notes.quote: Caleb Wilson, honestly, at the moment, he projects to be maybe the number two rookie

player_notes.text: Hayes sees him clearly ahead of Patrick Williams in the rotation.
player_notes.quote: I think Leonard Miller is ahead of Patrick Williams in the rotation.

player_notes.text: He is an active two-way player who crashes the glass and can play the 3, 4 and 5.
player_notes.quote: how he did crash the glass and like you said, you play three positions

player_notes.text: He projects as about the third player off the bench, behind Tre Jones and Jalen Smith, and would likely start if Buzelis or Wilson got hurt.
player_notes.quote: Trey Jones, Jaylen Smith, and Leonard Miller may be that next third guy off the bench

player_notes.text: Hayes ranks him behind Leonard Miller in the rotation.
player_notes.quote: I think Leonard Miller is ahead of Patrick Williams in the rotation.

player_notes.quote: he can make Jaylen Smith kind of expendable

player_notes.text: Hayes calls him a really good facilitator.
player_notes.quote: they have Trey Jones who's also a really good facilitator

team_notes.quote: If if they lose a Giddy or Bazalis or whoever it is, I think if they lost Claxton, they might be okay
